item: The library generation's state has no lock of its own: its four names are written only inside the exclusive window, and a pin keeps every writer reached only from inside one
refs: PR #1459; coordinator 17 Oct (option D of the close-window plan)
summary: library_generation guarded _GENERATION, _VALID, _WINDOW_STAMP and _DISK_CHANGED with a plain threading.Lock, _STATE. Every writer runs on the thread that holds the exclusive window and no reader ever took the lock, so it excluded nothing; its one effect was that a failed exit of a with on it (a 3-tuple allocation on 3.13) leaves it held and every later section of the same swap or the next waits behind it with the window held (4 of 5 sections of a swap that changes the disk could block that swap's own close, 3 of 4 for one refused before it, and the last one the next swap). _STATE and its five with blocks are now gone, so the failed-exit class for the state is removed, not shrunk; the release call and the window's own with self._lock sections are sites of the same kind and are untouched. The proof was an inventory (writers, readers, paths outside the window); its executable form is an AST pin over src/ that fails a call of bump, disk_changing, _open_window or _close_window made outside the body of a with ...swap_window(...) block or, in the module, outside the part of swap_window that holds the window (after _LOCK.exclusive returns, or in the cleanup behind held_here()); a writer referenced without being called; getattr or setattr by name; a store to the four names in any form, or a global of them from anything that is not a writer; found through every import form of src/ (absolute, relative, bare). It does not see a module reached by a computed name, and scripts/ is outside it. The independent read of the first version moved the reset of the flag above the acquire: that pin and four other test files passed, and run with two threads the earlier connections came back valid after a disk change (valid set [-1, 0, 1] against [1]); that placement is now a red-without both as a rewrite of the real source and as the two-thread run. The pin also fails a with or a module-level Lock in a writer or in a helper a writer calls. The instruction sweep gains a variant that calls disk_changing() in the body and asserts that after a MemoryError at any instruction of the cleanup only the new generation is valid; run in count mode it reaches the same sites as before (8, 6, 6 and 6 for the four combinations): the deleted with lines were never sites. Red-without: a synthetic source with the lock, with a call outside the window, with a reference, with a reset above the acquire, and a rewrite of the cleanup that decides the flag in a step of its own. tests/test_gates_survive_an_interrupt.py is untouched (its one test that injected through _STATE already injects at bump). Not changed: bump's two stores are not atomic against an interrupt (the lock never made them so); each server of a shared data folder has its own state and window.
